sourceObservations: You can set your working location in Google Calendar so collaborators know where you are and can easily find time to meet. Calendar automatically detects the relevant time zone and suggests meeting times that match where you work.

If you don't get an option to set your working location, your administrator may not have this feature enabled for your organization. Some working location features, such as specific addresses and automatic time zone updates, may not be available due to your organization's data compliance and location restrictions. Learn how to contact your administrator .
To set a working location, you need to have an eligible Google Workspace edition:
Important: To set a working location, turn on working hours. Learn how to set your working hours .
Tip: To change your working location, go to a specific day on your calendar and click the location chip. You can apply the change to that specific day or set it to repeat weekly.

sources.title: Change event & task visibility on your calendar
sourceObservations: In Google Calendar, you can change the visibility of individual events and tasks to control what others can find.
The "Default visibility" setting follows the main sharing settings for your calendar.
If you share your calendar with colleagues and give them the "See event details" permission or higher, they can find details about your event.
However, if you only share your calendar with "See free/busy" permission, they will only see you as busy.
To change the main sharing settings for your calendar, learn how to choose what others can do with your calendar .
